title: Specialist joint surface: does each domain's OWN atoms x data surface rise super-additively, mirroring the global M117 surface?

device._note: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1, gfx1201; A5/M119-exact specialist encode on GPU, ridge on CPU.

parity_guard.feature: CLS token concatenated with the mean of the patch tokens

sparse.specialist_construction: A5 exact: per-domain random whitened-patch candidates, seeded permutation pick (seed [11,100]), atoms = prefix of that permutation (nested: 256 is a prefix of 512, mirroring M117's nested atoms)
sparse.head: closed_form_ridge_1.0

scaling.subsample_rule: first n rows of each domain's train rows (n = round(fraction * n_d), nested)

gate.kill_switch_specialist_superadditive: per domain, at cell (256, 0.4*n_d): joint gain Q(512,n_d) - Q(256,0.4*n_d) must exceed the sum of the single-axis gains [Q(512,0.4*n_d)-Q(256,0.4*n_d)] + [Q(256,n_d)-Q(256,0.4*n_d)] by the M117 margin +0.005. KS FIRED if super-additivity holds on FEWER than 4 of 6 domains. Mirrors M117 (global surface was super-additive by +0.0097/+0.0101). If specialists are super-additive per domain, the specialist route is the primary buy-back candidate (cheap + scales + per-domain).
gate.registered_prediction: M119 showed specialists inherit per-domain data scaling at 512 atoms. If the per-domain joint surface is super-additive like the global one, more atoms use the domain's data productively and the specialist route to the buy-back is strongest.
